full_judgment: 4. The plaintiffs case, in brief, is that the suit property was declared abandoned property as per provision of P.O.16/72 and that defendant Nos. 1-2 have been in possession of the suit property by taking lease from defendant No. 3, the Government of Bangladesh. On taking decision to sell the suit property to the plaintiff, defendant No.1 on 22.10.1993 received Tk. 52,000/- out of the total consideration money of Tk. 2,37,000/- and thereafter, on 25.10.1993, defendant No.1 further received a sum of Tk. 85,000/- and thus in total he received Tk. 1,37,000/- as earnest money and executed a 'sikritinama' on that date admitting that when the Government would transfer the suit property in his favour then he would execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff on receipt of the balance consideration money. In the agreement for sale (sikritinama) instead of old khatian and present khatian Nos. 2351 and 1956 respectively the defendant mentioned khatian No. 15/2054 but the quantum of land, plot number, Mouza and house number were correctly written. At the time of obtaining registration from the government, the defendant informed the plaintiff that a further sum of Tk. 12,700/- for purchasing stamp, Tk. 13,000/- for office expenses and Tk. 15,000/- for personal expenses was necessary and that on 11.02.1994, the plaintiff paid the total sum of Tk. 40,700/- and thus total payment of earnest money stood at Tk. 1, 77,700/-. The Government transferred the suit property in favour of defendant No. 1 on 12.06.1994 and he became absolute owner of the suit property. After that, the plaintiff requested defendant Nos. 1-2 to execute and register the sale deed in favour of him on receipt of the balance consideration money but on various pretexts the defendants did not execute the deed of sale. Defendant No. 1 through his lawyer issued a legal notice upon plaintiff making some false statements and the plaintiff called a salish against issuance of false legal notice on 18.08.1994, defendant No. 1 with the object of grabbing the suit property trans ferried 5 decimals of land out of the suit land through registered heba-bil-ewaj deed in favour of his wife, defendant No. 2 and the plaintiff again called a salish on 20.1.1995 through the local people at the house of defendant No. 1 and in that salish plaintiff and defendant No. 1 gave written undertaking to accept the decision of the salish. After that, on 26.01.1995; the sat-shears again sat for decision and gave a written verdict stating that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 would execute and register the deed of sale in favour of plaintiff but defendant Nos. 1 and 2 did not do so. Last on 28.2.1995, defendant Nos. 1-2 refused to execute and register the also deed on receipt of balance consideration money of Tk. 59,300/- and as such the plaintiff was compelled to file the title suit for specific performance of contract.
